title: Restore ruff 0.16 lint compatibility
outOfScope: Changing the ruff 0.16.0 dependency pin, Python 3.11 baseline, runtime behavior, release state, or the dependency-refresh Work Item evidence.

Applying unsafe ruff fixes, weakening lint rules, or suppressing errors without a separately evidenced compatibility rationale; only the seven named rollback, fail-closed read, and optional-observability boundaries may retain a documented per-line BLE001 exception.
Merging, closing, rebasing, or deleting PR #481 or the stale Dependabot PRs during this corrective Work Item.

sources.reason: The parent replacement Work Item introduced the ruff 0.16.0 direct development pin.
Defines the repository lint configuration and must not be weakened as a shortcut.
PR #481 template-smoke ran make quality and reported the lint failure.
Records the serial Dependabot intake and pre-release remediation order.
Provides the bidirectional record for the parent dependency-refresh Work Item.

riskAssessment.reason: ruff 0.16.0 exposes 430 existing lint errors across scripts and tests on the parent PR; automatic fixes can be broad and must remain behavior-preserving and separately reviewable.

executionDecision.reason: The user authorized continuous corrective work; the observed hosted lint failure defines a bounded compatibility repair.

preReviewWarnings: Review that every mechanical change is a ruff 0.16.0-compatible lint correction and that no unsafe fix, rule suppression, or behavior change is introduced.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: ruff 0.16.0 project-lint completes with no errors using the existing repository configuration, without unsafe fixes or rule suppression.
Each changed script or test is a behavior-preserving lint or format compatibility correction; focused regression tests covering modified modules pass.
The corrective Contract, Summary, Capability Truth evidence, and instruction traceability record the hosted root cause and independent remediation without changing capability statuses.

A deterministic ruff 0.16 compatibility regression test is explicitly associated with every lint-corrected module that has no module-specific test-diff association; the coverage guard remains fail-closed and no generic test wildcard is added.
A fresh hosted run of the remediation PR has every required check successful, and then the parent #481 branch has every required check successful on its exact current Head before merge.
guidelines: Use only safe ruff fixes or explicit equivalent edits; do not use --unsafe-fixes or add blanket noqa/ignore suppressions. A per-line BLE001 annotation is allowed only for a named fail-safe rollback, fail-closed read, or optional-observability boundary where narrowing the caught exception would lose recovery or diagnostics.
Keep the correction behavior-preserving and limited to files reported by ruff 0.16.0; add or update focused tests if an edit changes executable logic.
Do not treat the parent PR's failed hosted run as successful evidence; require fresh hosted evidence for both the corrective and parent PRs.

intent.problem: PR #481 updated ruff to 0.16.0 and its required template-smoke failed because project-lint reports 430 pre-existing style and modernization errors. The failure is a direct compatibility consequence of the new tool version, not evidence that the dependency update is invalid.
constraints: Retain ruff 0.16.0, the existing Python 3.11 baseline, and the repository's lint policy; do not weaken rules to make CI green.

Use safe mechanical fixes only and preserve runtime behavior; do not use --unsafe-fixes, broad exclusions, or blanket noqa/ignore entries. The seven identified BLE001 boundaries may use narrowly documented per-line annotations because their recovery and diagnostic guarantees require catching every ordinary exception.
Do not run local make quality or full pytest under the user's temporary focused-verification direction; run targeted ruff and affected tests locally, while hosted required checks remain mandatory.
Keep this as an independent corrective Work Item and PR stacked onto #481; do not modify the archived dependency Work Item.
intent.rationale: A separate corrective record makes the tool-upgrade compatibility work reviewable, prevents disguising a broad source rewrite as a dependency bump, and preserves the parent dependency Work Item's evidence boundary.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: The user authorized the scoped corrective Work Item and its evidence updates after the observed hosted failure.

rollbackNote: Revert this Work Item diff and restore related tests and docs.

scenarioCoverage.expected: ruff check reports the same baseline classes of errors and the focused corrective test records the compatibility boundary.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run the ruff 0.16.0 project-lint command before and after the correction, preserving the failed-run evidence in the Summary.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Safe lint and formatting corrections leave affected behavior covered by focused tests.
scenarioCoverage.expected: ruff format --check and ruff check pass, and focused tests for every executable module changed by the correction pass.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Classify changed files, run ruff checks, and run the corresponding focused test groups after edits.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The corrective PR and its parent use fresh hosted evidence instead of the failed parent run or old Dependabot checks.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The corrective PR passes its hosted checks, then #481 is re-run and passes on the parent branch's updated Head.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Inspect both provider runs by PR Head SHA before either PR is merged.

declaredIntent.summary: Repair the ruff 0.16.0 compatibility regression revealed by fresh hosted CI without weakening evidence, lint, or release governance.
